**Eight practitioner assumptions, negated**

1. Stacked convs compose receptive fields, so an upstream conv makes a downstream conv more valuable. *Negated:* upstream conv already supplies the capacity, so a downstream conv is redundant (lower), or a stacked 1x1 adds nothing.
2. A parallel skip_connect is an additive optimization aid. *Negated:* the skip substitutes for what a conv adds into the same node, so conv edits are worth less.
3. avg_pool_3x3 is just a weak op. *Negated:* a pool edge supplies low-pass smoothing that complements conv/1x1 mixing (higher), and conv followed by pool is the classic pairing.
4. Pruning an edge hurts unless a strong sibling exists, and any strong sibling is equally good. *Negated:* a 1x1 sibling cannot replace the spatial aggregation of a removed 3x3-capable path, so pruning is more harmful, while a sibling 3x3 makes pruning nearly free.
5. 3x3 is uniformly better than 1x1. *Negated:* a 3x3 added next to another 3x3 into the same node saturates capacity and gains less.
6. A direct input-to-output edge (edge 3) is a safe shortcut that makes other edits unnecessary. *Negated:* a conv on edge 3 or a pool on it changes how much other edits help.
7. Edits on late edges (4, 5) matter most and early edges are interchangeable. *Negated:* early convs gain more when a downstream skip passes their features undistorted to the output.
8. Effects are dataset-specific. *Negated:* the interactions above are structural and appear consistently across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet16-120.
